title: RHiOTS: A Framework for Evaluating Hierarchical Time Series Forecasting Algorithms

problem.claim: Hierarchical time series forecasting models and algorithms need robustness assessment across diverse data conditions while preserving the hierarchical relationship between lower- and upper-level forecasts.

gap.claim: Existing empirical evaluations often use only a small set of benchmark datasets, providing a narrow view of algorithm behavior.

contributions.claim: RHiOTS is a framework for evaluating the robustness of hierarchical time series forecasting models and algorithms on real-world datasets.
The framework systematically alters existing datasets and individual series characteristics and interrelations using parameterizable transformations that simulate changes in data distribution.
RHiOTS includes a visualization component for representing multidimensional robustness evaluation results in interpretable visuals.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report using RHiOTS to analyze the predictive performance of several algorithms.
The authors find that conventional statistical approaches generally withstand the transformations better than leading deep-learning methods, unless the transformation is highly disruptive.
The authors report no significant robustness differences when applying specific reconciliation methods such as MinT.

narrative_sequence.summary: Hierarchical time series require lower-level forecasts to sum to upper-level forecasts and occur in contexts such as retail across countries.
Current evaluations rely on few benchmark datasets and provide a narrow view of algorithm behavior.
RHiOTS varies datasets, series characteristics, and interrelations through parameterizable transformations and provides multidimensional result visualizations.
The framework is used to examine the predictive performance and robustness of several algorithms under diverse conditions.

Traditional statistical methods are reported as more robust than deep learning methods except under highly disruptive transformations, with no significant differences for certain reconciliation methods.

source_observation.claim: Systematically transforming existing datasets can expose algorithm behavior under diverse data-distribution conditions.

interpretation.claim: Robustness evaluation can benefit from controlled variation of both individual series and their interrelations rather than relying only on fixed benchmarks.

application.claim: Use parameterizable data transformations to stress-test forecasting methods across controlled changes in distribution and hierarchical structure.

exception.claim: The reported robustness ordering changes when the transformation effect is highly disruptive.

source_observation.claim: The framework converts complex multidimensional robustness results into intuitive visuals.

interpretation.claim: Interpretability of evaluation outputs may help researchers compare nuanced algorithm behavior across conditions.

application.claim: Pair robustness experiments with visual summaries that make multidimensional performance differences easier to inspect.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify which visualization designs or user contexts are effective.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the real-world datasets or forecasting algorithms evaluated.
The abstract does not specify the transformation parameters, reconciliation methods beyond MinT, or statistical significance procedure.
The abstract does not quantify the reported performance or robustness differences.
